summary: MySeliaSan is now a downloadable, installable product on the r450k download page, packaged to full parity with MyMataSan: portable archives (linux/windows/darwin x amd64/arm64), .deb and .rpm packages that install to /opt/myseliasan with a systemd unit and a dedicated service user, a Windows Inno Setup installer that registers a service and generates a one-time admin password, and multi-arch GHCR Docker images. It is pure Go - no ffmpeg, no Python, no model weights - so the payload is just the binary, the web UI and a default config. myseliasan releases under its OWN tag namespace (myseliasan-v<ver>) and is published with --latest=false, so it is versioned and released independently of mymatasan (a bump to either ships that product alone) and never becomes the repo's 'latest' release, which mymatasan's in-app updater reads. GoReleaser OSS cannot derive a semver from a prefixed tag (monorepo/tag_prefix is a Pro feature), so the release workflow hands it a plain version via GORELEASER_CURRENT_TAG, disables its GitHub-release step, and publishes with 'gh release create' itself. The r450k download page now resolves the newest release per product from separate tags (it can no longer use /releases/latest, which only ever returns mymatasan's) and renders a download block per product. Also fixed a packaging blocker: myseliasan's RegisterWebRoutes resolved static/index.html from the CWD-relative BaseDir() rather than deps.HomeDir, so a packaged install (binary and static/ side by side, service working directory elsewhere) would have 404'd on / and /index.html. The self-signed certificate the app generates on first boot is now issued for the running app instead of always claiming CommonName=mymatasan.
compatibility: No schema or config changes for existing installs. The shipped distribution config (deploy/dist/myseliasan-config.json) differs from the dev config in ways that matter when packaging: it defaults to SQLite rather than Postgres, ships no secrets (an empty jwt.secret is generated on first boot), leaves sso.providerBaseUrl empty so a standalone install runs on local accounts only, and uses the 4953x pairing ports - which are the MyMataSan shipped defaults - rather than the 3953x ports used in development. Operators must set pairing.parentBaseUrl to a LAN-reachable URL for the host before adopting nodes: nodes store it and dial back to it, so leaving it as localhost silently breaks adoption from another machine. secret/atrest.key in the data dir encrypts the fleet CA key and pairing PSK and must be backed up with the database; the packages deliberately preserve the data dir on remove.
